title: AI pose-recognition home exercise program improves walking distance and systolic blood pressure in adults with hypertension in Guangzhou
summary: In a 62-person Guangzhou trial, 8 weeks of AI pose-guided home exercise added 62.77 m to 6-minute walk distance and lowered systolic pressure more than usual care.
account: Researchers at Zhujiang Hospital of Southern Medical University, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital and the Hong Kong Polytechnic University tested home exercise guided by an AI app for adults with hypertension. They recruited 62 patients in Guangzhou from November 2023 to October 2024 and randomized them to the app or to conventional offline exercise guidance, with health education in both groups. The app, from RaphAI Health Technologies Limited, used OpenPose pose estimation on the phone camera to track 17 body points and give corrective feedback during sessions. Patients trained at least three times a week for eight weeks. The app group gained 62.77 meters more in the 6-minute walk test than the control group. Its systolic blood pressure fell by 4.11 mmHg more, and diastolic pressure did not differ. No serious adverse events related to the program occurred. The trial was small and open-label, and it used convenience sampling.
purpose: The app was built to guide and correct home rehabilitation exercise. The gains in fitness and blood pressure follow from that purpose.
